messages:
Ivy: Hey team, first day and hitting a few weird bootstrap issues on my new M2 laptop. Installed Homebrew to /opt/homebrew, installed asdf, set fish as my shell. Terminal.app shows everything working but in VSCode's integrated terminal `asdf` is missing. Any quick checks?

Rashid: welcome! VSCode tends to spawn non-login shells. For fish add the brew path early in ~/.config/fish/config.fish: `set -x PATH /opt/homebrew/bin /opt/homebrew/sbin $PATH`. Also source asdf: `source /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.fish` (path may vary).

Marta: another gotcha: if you use direnv, put `eval (direnv hook fish)` after PATH so project envs get the right libs.

Ivy: added those lines. Now asdf is visible but `asdf install ruby 3.1.2` fails: `openssl/evp.h` not found. Brew's openssl is installed.

Rashid: many native builds need LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS for brew libs on mac-arm. In fish do: `set -x LDFLAGS '-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib'` and `set -x CPPFLAGS '-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include'` before running asdf install. If plugin expects openssl@3 adjust path.

Ivy: added flags, ruby build progressed. Next: trying `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` fails with gpg errors during verification.

Marta: run the nodejs plugin key import: ```bash
bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring
``` If gpg complains about keyring write permissions set `export GNUPGHOME=$HOME/.gnupg-asdf` first.

Ivy: that fixed the gpg step. Thanks. One more: trying to push to git from VSCode produced "Permission denied (publickey)". I use 1Password for SSH keys. VSCode didn't forward my host agent.

Rashid: forwarding can be flaky. Two patterns: host-forwarding or container-local agent. For host-forwarding, ensure `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is exported in the environment VSCode inherits, and enable agent forwarding in your remote config. For a cleaner approach, we run 1Password signin and add inside the container/shell: `eval (op signin --sh)` then `op item get <ssh-key> --attributes privateKey | ssh-add -`.

Ivy: is it safe to evaluate `op signin` in my interactive shell rc? I don't want tokens lingering.

Marta: better to use a tiny helper script that checks for a valid OP_SESSION and only signs in when needed. We have `dotfiles/scripts/op-ensure-session` that does: `if not op whoami; then eval (op signin --sh); fi`. For ssh keys it runs `op item get <id> --attributes privateKey | ssh-add -` and ensures `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` points to a stable socket like `~/.ssh/agent.sock`. Ping me and I can share.

Rashid: small fish tips: use `eval (op signin --sh)` (no $) and to clear fish command cache after reshim do `functions -c sh -s` just kidding — actually run `hash -r` to clear the command lookup cache in fish.

Ivy: ha thanks. After running the helper and adding the key git push works from VSCode. One last odd thing: `asdf reshim` created new npm shims but my current tab still invokes the old binary until I open a new tab; `hash -r` fixed it.

Marta: yep. Also ensure `~/.asdf/shims` is before other bin dirs in PATH so shims win.

Ivy: awesome, all green now. Appreciate the fast help! :smile:
